_doc: PATH-KEYING EXEMPTIONS. See scripts/check_path_keying.py for what this
gates and why -- three separator defects (check_swift_copy_sites.py,
genericity_check.py, check_element_dispatch.py), each fixed as an
instance, none of them as a class.
A row excuses ONE rendering of a path to text. Keyed
'relpath::expression' -- the git-tracked POSIX relpath and the expression
source, NEVER the line number, which moves when unrelated code moves.
Run the gate to see the exact key it wants; it prints file, line and
expression for every finding.
EVERY ROW NEEDS A NON-EMPTY `reason`. A blank one excuses nothing AND
hides nothing -- the gate reports the missing reason and still reports the
site (self-test case (y), which caught the opposite behaviour in this
gate's first draft).
A row matching no current finding is STALE and reds. That arm is not
tidiness. `swift:dropdown` in widget_dispatch_exemptions.json asserted two
things that had been false for months, and on 2026-07-29 a seat read the
row, believed it, and set out to build what already shipped. A declared
exception that outlives its condition reads as a decision nobody has
rechecked.
Before adding a row, check that neither ordinary answer applies:
* the text is DATA (a key, a baseline row, a regex subject, anything
written to a file another platform will read) -> `.as_posix()`;
* the text is an ARGUMENT to the OS (`open`, `read_text`, `subprocess`)
-> pass the Path itself, which is what every call site here already
does -- `subprocess.run([...], cwd=REPO)` needs no rendering at all.
A rendering that is neither of those is rare enough to be worth writing a
sentence about, which is the entire mechanism.
Note that a message read by a human -- `print`, `sys.stderr.write`, a
`logging` call, `warnings.warn`, a `raise`, an `assert` message -- needs NO
exemption. Native separators are correct there: the reader is on the
platform that produced them. There are nine such sites in the tree and
none of them belong in this file.
